text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents original research focused on predicting future land use and land cover change (LULCC) at the national scale of mainland Tanzania. It implements two distinct future scenarios—business as usual (BAU) and green economy (GE)—with quantitative comparisons of LULCC outcomes, including mapped spatial projections (e.g., Figures 3 and 4). The modeling integrates stakeholder-driven inputs with national spatial datasets to produce spatially explicit, quantitative outputs (e.g., km² of cropland expansion, degradation areas). The study explicitly covers the entire mainland Tanzania (~883,600 km²), uses a reference land cover map (MNRT 2013), and reports quantitative metrics such as annual expansion rates (~2% per year), absolute area changes (e.g., 44,132 km² cropland increase under GE), and degradation extents. All core inclusion criteria are met: national-scale implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with quantitative outputs, and inclusion of mapped projections. None of the exclusion criteria apply.)
